why: I compared each of the seven checks' PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests only exit=0 and a byte-exact cmp of `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]\n`, which is what line 1 says. Checks 2–5 test only byte-exact output and don't add an exit-code test the lines don't state. Check 5's `printf '[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n'` correctly produces the JSON tab escape. Check 6 requires `npm test` to exit 0 plus a test that runs the CLI with --tsv on tab input and "asserts on its stdout", which matches "checks its output". Check 7 requires only that the flag is described and an example uses it. "such as `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`" is only an illustration. The stricter items (other arguments alongside the flag, README saying "tab-separated", no quoting/--sep/--help) all sit under "Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL)". None of the checks adds a stricter requirement.
